comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C3-C4, C50-C55 regarding the derivation of temporal discounting function from reward-rate optimization. Both evaluations find the mathematical derivation valuable and well-supported. Reviewer 3 explicitly appreciates this derivation as providing evidence for equivalence between reward rate optimization and hyperbolic discounting.

Perfect agreement on claims C5-C6, C56-C58, C98 regarding the framework's ability to explain behavioral phenomena as consequences of optimal behavior. Both evaluations recognize this as a valuable contribution that provides a unifying framework for seemingly contradictory empirical observations.

Disagreement on claims C2, C39-C41 regarding subjective value and apportionment cost. OpenEval finds the mathematical derivations rigorous and valid. Peer reviewers acknowledge improvements but Reviewer 3 notes apportionment cost 'remains hard to intuit' and the additive form 'doesn't add much in way of intuition,' indicating conceptual clarity concerns despite mathematical validity.

Disagreement on claims C7, C62-C63, C68 regarding the Malapportionment Hypothesis. OpenEval finds the systematic analysis rigorous and the logic sound. Peer Reviewer 3 raises critical questions about the mechanistic origin of malapportionment and notes the lack of discussion on dissociating underestimation and overestimation, suggesting the hypothesis needs further development.

Strong agreement on claims C30-C31, C59-C61 regarding established empirical findings showing optimal forgo but suboptimal choice behavior. Both evaluations recognize this as well-supported by literature. Peer review also includes C69 and explicitly praises the explanation of these behavioral inconsistencies as a key contribution.

Strong agreement on claims C93-C97 regarding testable predictions from the framework. Both evaluations find these predictions logically valid and well-derived from the theoretical framework. Peer review also includes C70-C72 and confirms these follow from the framework without challenge.

Agreement on claims C82, C84-C85 regarding critiques of standard hyperbolic models. Both evaluations accept the theoretical analysis showing standard models lack the opportunity cost term. Peer review also includes C90-C91 and recognizes the value of the unifying framework without challenging these specific critiques.

Agreement on claims C70-C72 regarding predictions from the Malapportionment Hypothesis. Both evaluations find these predictions logically follow from the framework. Note that while peer R7 supports these specific predictions, peer R4 expresses uncertainty about the broader Malapportionment Hypothesis itself (C7, C62-C63, C68).

Agreement on claims C90-C91 regarding methodological observations about real versus hypothetical delays. OpenEval notes empirical support from Jimura et al. 2009 and sound theoretical explanation. Peer reviewers accept the theoretical framework's critiques of existing models without challenging these specific methodological points.

OpenEval finds claims C1, C8 regarding reward-rate maximization as a normative principle well-supported as established scientific consensus. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational claims.
